claimed_edges.evidence: src/flask/__init__.py imports `from . import json as json` at module level.
src/flask/json/__init__.py imports `from ..globals import current_app` at module level.

src/flask/globals.py imports `from .app import Flask` only inside `if t.TYPE_CHECKING:`, which the interpreter never executes. Its runtime imports are __future__, typing, contextvars (ContextVar) and werkzeug.local (LocalProxy); the globals are LocalProxy objects over a ContextVar, so no Flask class is needed at import time. This is the edge a naive text search for `from .app import` reports as real.
src/flask/app.py does not import flask.json at all, not even under a type-checking guard.

root_cause: There is no circular import. Two of the four edges the triage notes claim do not exist at runtime, so the chain never closes: `from flask.json import dumps` imports cleanly on a pristine 3.1.0 and the reported blueprint scenario serves a normal response. The real cycles in flask are only the benign package<->submodule partial-initialisation ones that any re-exporting __init__.py has. The correct answer refutes the reported cycle and recommends no code change; the customer's ImportError has some other cause and needs their actual traceback.
_scoring_evidence_rationale: Tokens absent from every prompt the agent is shown (task.toml [[sessions]].prompt for this chain task, plus instruction.md) and present only in src/flask/globals.py, so a prompt echo cites none of them. Flat strings, one-for-one scored, because tests/integrity/test_scoring_evidence_is_nonprompt.py only walks string entries — a nested any-of shape would be silently skipped and the non-prompt invariant would stop covering this task. Each survives lowercased substring matching: type_checking matches TYPE_CHECKING, contextvar matches ContextVar and contextvars, werkzeug matches werkzeug.local. resolution_correct grades only type_checking: a refusal to patch that cannot name the guard does not actually know why the edge is not real.
_residual_risk: CLOSED-BOOK, not closable here (rryas precedent): a model that knows Flask internals may write that globals.py proxies via werkzeug LocalProxy over contextvars without reading the repo, and may know the Flask import in globals.py sits under a TYPE_CHECKING guard. The discrimination checkpoint is the defence that does not depend on those tokens — the four CLAIMED edges are invented for this task, so no prior tells an agent which two are real. GUESSING, measured by exhaustive enumeration rather than asserted: negative marking makes every BLANKET answer score exactly 0, but random per-edge guessing is NOT worth zero in expectation — the max(0, ...) floor is required to keep a score in [0,1] and it clips losses without capping wins, so E[score] = 0.1875 over the 16 equiprobable guesses (0.075 of the task at weight 0.40) and P(all four right) = 1/16. Four edges is too few for any per-edge rule to suppress guessing further. Tolerable because a guesser earns ~0 on investigation_evidence and resolution_correct, which require evidence a non-reader does not have; the floor cannot be dropped without breaking the score contract.
